narrative:
On September 15, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 35.8%, taking up 1,027 of the 2,871 scheduled matters across 46 judges. This represents a noticeable decline compared to recent proceedings, dropping from 50.8% on September 11, 38.6% on September 10, and 44.2% on September 9. 

Courtroom throughput varied significantly across benches. Justice C.M. Poonacha demonstrated substantial clearance across heavy cause lists, hearing 90 of 126 matters (71.4%) in one session and 47 of 60 (78.3%) in another. Justice G. Basavaraja also maintained strong momentum, hearing 73 of 108 cases (67.6%), alongside Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde, who cleared 55 of 75 cases (73.3%). Conversely, substantial backlogs persisted in benches handling massive dockets; Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard only 1 of 279 matters in a primary list, while benches presided over by Justice K.V. Aravind (148 scheduled across two lists), Justice S.R. Krishna Kumar (54 scheduled), and Justice S. Rachaiah (47 scheduled) recorded no hearings.

Stage-wise analysis reveals that early-stage matters achieved the highest conversion. Cases listed for Admission saw the best progress among major categories, converting 53.6% (395 of 737), followed by Orders at 43.1% (326 of 757). In contrast, substantive determination lagged; Final Hearing matters achieved a 21.5% hearing rate (117 of 545)—down from over 30% on preceding days—while Further Hearing cases experienced severe bottlenecks, converting just 5.8% (19 of 326).

Writ Petitions constituted the largest share of the court's calendar with 1,486 listings, but posted a subdued clearance rate of 28.9% (429 heard), down sharply from 53.7% on September 11. Criminal matters exhibited stronger clearance, with Criminal Petitions converting 53.8% (197 of 366) and Criminal Appeals reaching 56.2% (82 of 146). Miscellaneous First Appeals saw moderate disposal at 41.8% (159 of 380), while Regular Second Appeals converted only 25.0% (38 of 152).
